items.title: Dev GUI tool
items.text:
Working features:

  • Load and parse format definition file
  • Show internal AST
  • Show generated serdes code
  • Show generated client-server code
  • no_std switch to quickly view how embedded vs host code looks like

Planned features:

  • Provide input and output widgets for various types (number with SI support as spinner / dial / slide, string, color, ...)
  • Generate documentation like UI with the ability to interact with server code
  • Generate server mockup UI with the ability to respond with user input, prerecorded answers or examples
  • Support for bytecode loading to extract types and api information
  • Support for source loading from external sources and compiling to bytecode (through Rust lib FFI or backend service)

items.title: WireWeaver features and roadmap
items.text: This file is the single source of truth for what WireWeaver supports, what is being worked on and what is planned, for humans and AI agents alike. It replaces the external task tracker.

items.title: How to use this file
items.text:
• Status of each item:
  • ✅ done
  • 🚧 in progress or partially done (the note says what is missing)
  • 📋 planned
  • 💡 idea, not committed to
  • ⛔ blocked (the note says on what)
  • 🔍 probably done or obsolete, needs a check before closing
  • 🧪 done and tested on the host, the check on hardware is still open (the note says what to check)
  • Target is the release an item is planned for: v0.5 is the next release (the workspace is at 0.5.0, crates.io has 0.4.0). v0.5.x is the next compatible release after it: v0.5.1 if nothing turns out to be breaking, otherwise the next minor. No tag means not scheduled. grep 'v0.5' FEATURES.md gives the release scope.
  • IDs (SW-3, CLT-12) are stable: never renumber or reuse one. New items take the next free number of their area, even when they are inserted in the middle of it. Use the ID in commit messages, CHANGELOG entries and code TODOs (// TODO(SRV-4): ...). When talking to people, name an ID with a short slug from its title (SW-3 string-and-vec), never bare.
  • Items are grouped by area. Each area lists what works first (✅), then open items ordered by target.
  • When finishing work, update the item in the same change: mark it ✅, move it up to the done items of its area and add a pointer (docs page, crate, test or example). Don't delete done items. Move items that turn out to be obsolete to Dropped and superseded with a one-line reason.
  • This file is also rendered as the docs site's "Features" page (docs/features.md includes it), so indent nested lists and paragraphs inside an item by 4 spaces, as Python-Markdown requires.
  • New ideas go into the matching area as 💡. Small code-level gaps stay as TODO comments in the source; only those that limit users or block a feature get an item here.

items.title: Wire format (shrink_wrap, SW)
items.text:
• ✅ SW-1 Structs, plain enums and data enums, discriminant type selection with ww_repr.
  • ✅ SW-2 Option and Result, also inside Vec, as one-bit flags.
  • ✅ SW-3 String and Vec<T>, with special handling of Vec<u8>.
  • ✅ SW-4 Fixed size arrays, tuples and the unit type ().
  • ✅ SW-5 Bit-aligned integers: nibbles and u1..u32 (un); un8/un16 are forwarded to un32 for smaller flash.
  • ✅ SW-6 Variable length numbers: UNib32, UVlq32, and UVlq32Backfill for values known only after the rest is serialized.
  • ✅ SW-7 Borrowed and owned types: Sized and Unsized traits, RefStr/RefVec, borrowed types by default and Owned variants generated automatically.
  • ✅ SW-8 Evolvable by default: every struct and enum is Unsized; final_structure, self_describing and sized are opt-ins.
  • ✅ SW-9 TailBytes / TailBytesOwned: bytes that take up the rest of the buffer, written without a size; only valid as the last item. Generated API code puts them in place of byte slices, e.g. for return values and property values.
  • ✅ SW-10 EitherAnyVec: zero-copy, no-alloc array of Either elements of any types, with the L/R flags packed in groups of 8 instead of padding each element. Packs e.g. a list of Results tightly; used for multi-read and multi-call results (only multi-read exists so far).
  • ✅ SW-55 OptionAnyVec: zero-copy, no-alloc array of Option slots of any types (numbers, structs, lists, strings, a nested OptionAnyVec for a child level), only the present values written, in slot order without padding between them. A presence header up front in the smallest of four modes (all, dense bits, two-level bits, index list), self-delimiting so that readers with fewer or more slots than the writer read it (slots are only appended); a malformed header is an error. Writer takes the present set up front (SetBits over a bitset, any increasing iterator), OptionAnyVecWriter / in-place OptionAnyVecBuilder. For a trait level's properties in one update (API-38). See docs/serdes/shrink_wrap.md#optionanyvec-sparse-slots-of-any-types, docs/serdes/showcase.md.
  • ✅ SW-11 Alloc writer BufWriterOwned, SerializeShrinkWrap for &[u8], String as UFS.
  • ✅ SW-12 In-place builders used by the server codegen (event and error builders), and the manual patch-the-discriminant-later pattern (docs/serdes/showcase.md).
  • ✅ SW-13 Binary format documented in docs/serdes/shrink_wrap.md, worked tricks in docs/serdes/showcase.md.
  • ✅ SW-14 Usable standalone as a dense data storage format (examples/minimal_shrink_wrap, examples/compare_wire_formats).
  • ✅ SW-31 Delta / DeltaOfDelta: integer sequences as (differences of) differences in a bit-level prefix code, zero-copy Delta<'i, T> and DeltaOwned<T>, u8..u64 / i8..i64; the Gorilla timestamp code (docs/serdes/shrink_wrap.md, shrink_wrap/src/series/, shrink_wrap/tests/series.rs).
  • ✅ SW-32 XorFloat: f32 / f64 sequences as XOR with the previous value (Gorilla), bit-exact, XorFloat<'i, T> / XorFloatOwned<T> (same places as SW-31).
  • ✅ SW-50 Compressed sequences in APIs: Delta, DeltaOfDelta and XorFloat (borrowed or owned) in every API position (arguments, returns, properties, stream and sink items, fields of API types), visible in introspection (ww_self::Type::Delta / DeltaOfDelta / XorFloat, appended), read and written by the dynamic client and Python (lists of numbers); another codec or element type, or a plain Vec instead, is breaking (ww api check). tests/series, docs/types.md, docs/evolution/rules.md.
  • ✅ SW-34 Smaller code on small CPUs: BufReader / BufWriter reads and writes that keep an error instead of returning it (read_u8_latch, write_u32_latch, .., latched()), used by #[derive_shrink_wrap] for plain fields with one check per type; Error without payloads; one shared integer read and write; no division in UNib32. 19 to 20 % less code for a derived request/reply codec on RV32IC and Cortex-M0, same wire format. Numbers, where the rest goes and what is left to do: docs/serdes/code_size.md (measured by TEST-17).
  • ✅ SW-36 No length FIFO code for types without lengths: SerializeShrinkWrap::PUSHES_LEN, computed by #[derive_shrink_wrap] from the fields (default true unless Sized), lets to_ww_bytes and BufWriter::finish_for::<T>() end with finish_no_lens() at compile time, so the FIFO encoder is not linked: about 510 bytes less per such encoder on RV32IC (a struct of plain fields 1476 → 964). For types with lengths encode_len_fifo / write_nib are smaller (vec_ser 1378 → 1142). Same wire format (shrink_wrap/tests/pushes_len.rs, docs/serdes/code_size.md steps 4 and 5).
  • ✅ SW-37 RefVec of plain numbers without the decode pass: a list of u8..u128, i8..i128, f32 or f64 finds its end with one bounds check instead of reading every element (4096 bytes: 10 µs → 6 ns on a host), same result, errors and reader state as the pass, same wire format (shrink_wrap/tests/ref_vec_skip.rs, just fuzz-shrink-wrap-ref-vec). Costs 50 to 140 bytes of code in a decoder with such a list. Other Sized types keep the pass on purpose (stride is not size_bits, elements are validated there): docs/serdes/code_size.md.
  • ✅ SW-38 Latched reads of U1..U64 / I2..I64 fields: read like the integers of SW-34, with one error check per type (through a hidden DeserializeShrinkWrap::des_shrink_wrap_latch); a bit-packed struct decodes in 40 bytes less on RV32IC (886 → 846), 88 on RV32I. Same wire format, results and errors as reading field by field (shrink_wrap/tests/latched_reads.rs, just fuzz-shrink-wrap-latched). Nibble, u64 and varints are not latched: one such field costs more than it saves (docs/serdes/code_size.md).
  • ✅ SW-41 First error in types that mix latched and other fields: an error kept by a _latch read stops the reader (reads with a Result return it, no read moves), so a derived decoder with lists or nested types next to plain fields returns the first error again, as before SW-34. 20 bytes on a request/reply decoder (RV32IC), four forms measured (docs/serdes/code_size.md, shrink_wrap/tests/latched_errors.rs).
  • ✅ SW-43 C99 runtime (first step of API-26): shrink_wrap/c/shrink_wrap.{h,c}, the BufReader / BufWriter of the Rust crate for C: bits, nibbles, un8..un64, LE integers, floats, UNib32, UVlq32 / UVlq64, bytes and strings as borrowed views, split, lengths at the back and finish, Unsized values. No malloc, the first error kept as in SW-41 (a failing call moves nothing), octets through accessors so 16-bit char (TI C2000) works. Checked against the Rust crate with golden vectors and a proptest cross-check in both directions, also on truncated and corrupted input (shrink_wrap/c/tests, part of just test; just lint builds the C with -std=c99 -pedantic -Werror). How to use it: docs/c.md. TailSize, the series types and the _latch / finish_no_lens code size tricks are not ported.
  • ✅ SW-44 Fixed-layout fast path: #[derive_shrink_wrap] sees when a type's encoding is a fixed little-endian byte layout (a sized or final_structure struct, a sized or self_describing enum with a u8 / u16 / u32 ww_repr; fields only u8..u64, i8..i64, f32, f64 and arrays of them) and generates an offset const per field, ENCODED_LEN, and from_fixed / to_fixed that load and store at those offsets on the slice, no BufReader / BufWriter, nothing generic. The fixed_layout directive makes it a requirement (and allows nested fixed-layout types): a bool, Option, list, string, varint or bit-packed field is a compile error naming the field. Same bytes as ser_shrink_wrap (shrink_wrap/tests/fixed_layout.rs, 2000 random values per type). FixedLayout::write_c prints the matching C reader (offset defines and static inline loads) from the same derive, fixed_layout::write_c_header a whole header: the first generated C of API-26. Code size on Cortex-M0 for a header of eight integers: decode 484 → 276 bytes, encode 888 → 462 (docs/serdes/code_size.md). First user: chunky_mcu_updater's plan format (P2625 PROTO-3); it serves the busgen idea of P2401 #9oct-1433 for types without dynamic fields. Open: arrays of nested types, a C writer, 16-bit char targets in the C reader.
  • ✅ SW-45 Bit fields and a variable last field in the fixed-layout fast path: bool, U1..U32, I2..I32 and Nibble get compile-time bit offsets (most significant bit first, a Nibble on a 4-bit boundary, a byte field after them starting a fresh byte, as BufWriter packs them) and are read and written with shifts and masks, in Rust and in the C reader (sw_fixed_bits, sw_fixed_sbits). Option<T>, Result<T, E> and enums of unequal variants are allowed as the last field (one rule for all variable-length fields); their flags are bit fields, also where #[flag] moves them. MIN_LEN and fixed_len() next to ENCODED_LEN (the longest, the buffer to have ready). A nested type cannot share a byte with bits of its parent: a compile error says so. Every refusal says why and what to use instead. Byte-equal to ser_shrink_wrap on mixed bit runs, a run at the end, options, results, relocated flags and enum variants with both (shrink_wrap/tests/fixed_layout.rs); the generated C is built and run with every warning an error (just lint-c). A bit-packed sample on Cortex-M0: decode 652 → 276 bytes, encode 1034 → 560.
  • ✅ SW-46 Fixed head, sequential tail (head_tail): an opt-in wire format of its own for types with lists, strings and options anywhere. The head holds every fixed-width field at a constant offset (numbers, arrays, bit fields as in SW-45) plus a u16 count per list or string, the flag bit of each Option / Result and the head of each nested type; the tail holds the variable parts in field order. An enum is its tag, then its variant's head and tail. Generated by #[derive_shrink_wrap(head_tail)]: offset consts, HEAD_LEN, from_head_tail / to_head_tail / head_tail_len, the HeadTail trait (also implemented for every fixed-layout type) and a C reader (head readers plus a <name>_tail() walker, shrink_wrap::head_tail::write_c_header), built and run by just lint-c. Non-generic, size first: no BufReader / BufWriter, no length FIFO, no reversed lengths; the tail is a cursor (head_tail::Tail) that takes lengths it already knows. Lists are head_tail::List<'i, T> (items numbers or fixed-layout types of one length, read when iterated). No sw serdes and no owned version: one type, one format. Tests: exact bytes, round trips, every truncation, 200 000 random buffers, UTF-8, counts over u16 (shrink_wrap/tests/head_tail.rs). busgen's request and reply enums (size bench busgen_ht): 4626 bytes on Cortex-M0 and 6004 on RV32IC, against 4408 / 5762 hand-written and 6652 / 8210 derived (P2401 #9oct-1433). Open: head_tail types as ww API arguments (they have no sw serdes), lists of variable-length items, a C writer, u8 counts for short lists (MaxLen).
  • ✅ SW-52 head_tail views and variant writers: Type::view(buf) gives a TypeView<'_> without making the value: the lengths checked and the tail walked once, the head's fields read by accessors at their offsets when called (the same code as from_head_tail, one field at a time), lists, strings, options and nested views kept from the walk; an enum's view is an enum of its variants' views (a tuple variant of one nested type holds its view). Every enum variant gets Enum::write_<variant>(buf, fields..): the bytes of to_head_tail for that variant without making the value (the same write_ht code). HeadTail::View / view_ht, head_tail::view. Tests: values back from every accessor, writers byte-equal to to_head_tail, every truncation, 200 000 random buffers agreeing with from_head_tail. Size bench busgen_view: 4988 bytes on RV32IC and 3894 on Cortex-M0, 13 % and 12 % below the hand-written codec; busgen's firmware 5608 / 5090 bytes (UART / I2C image, fpga_tools BUS-12). View types are always pub (the View of a public trait). Open: lazy views of nested fixed-layout types (read when the view is made), a writer for structs.
  • ✅ SW-53 Numbers through fixed_layout::Le, out of line on RISC-V: generated fixed-layout and head_tail code reads and writes multi-byte numbers with Le::ld / Le::st on the bytes at the field (fixed_layout::at), one function per type on RISC-V (no unaligned loads), inline elsewhere (on Cortex-M0 the byte loads are smaller than the calls, measured). Under LTO ld passes its pointer through black_box: argument promotion would otherwise move the load into every caller. Bit-field bytes cleared once per head. busgen_ht on RV32IC 6004 → 5658; a type read or written in one place grows (fixed_ser 498 → 612, docs/serdes/code_size.md).
  • ✅ SW-54 #[cfg] on head_tail enum variants: passed to everything generated for the variant (consts, arms, view, writer, C text); a variant compiled out keeps its tag and reads as an unknown one. busgen's firmware builds only its bitstream family's requests with it.
  • ✅ SW-39 Byte-wise memcpy, measured, advice for very small targets: a firmware's own memcpy (and __aeabi_memcpy on Arm) of 22 bytes instead of the word-wise one of compiler_builtins: 324 bytes less on RV32IC, 304 on Cortex-M0, for every image that moves a value, at the price of speed and of replacing memcpy for the whole firmware. Code and downsides in docs/serdes/code_size.md ("Build settings"), measured with just size-bench --fw-features byte_memcpy. Nothing in shrink_wrap depends on it.
  • ✅ SW-40 Bit reads stay out of the lengths in the last byte: read_un8..read_un64 (and U1..U64, I2..I64) no longer read into the length nibble the last byte shares with the forward data, and a length is no longer read from bits the forward side has read; both are OutOfBounds.. errors. Malformed input only, every message the writers produce decodes as before. Checked against a bit-level model in every reader state of 1 to 3 byte buffers (buf_reader.rs bounds_every_state_every_read) and by round trips of random messages (shrink_wrap/tests/rev_nibble_bounds.rs).
  • ✅ SW-35 Exact ElementSize of enums: a sized / self_describing enum reports the discriminant plus one variant (ElementSize::one_of) instead of the sum of all variants without the discriminant; sized with variants of different sizes is a compile error; user types inside arrays, tuples, ranges and options are counted. Same wire format (shrink_wrap/tests/enum_size.rs, docs/serdes/derive.md). Unblocks reading RefVec<Sized T> in place.
  • ✅ SW-33 UVlq64: byte-based variable length u64, same big endian VLQ encoding as UVlq32, 1 to 10 bytes, uvlq64 field type in #[derive_shrink_wrap(..)], BufReader::read_uvlq64/BufWriter/BufWriterOwned::write_uvlq64 (shrink_wrap/src/vlq64.rs, docs/types.md, docs/serdes/showcase.md). No UVlq64Backfill (not asked for).
  • ✅ SW-19 Bounded lists and strings MaxLen<T, N>: a RefVec, Vec, &str or String with at most N elements, same bytes as T (a bound can be added, raised or removed without a new wire form), checked on serialize and deserialize (Error::MaxLenExceeded, never truncated). Works in derived types and in every API position (arguments, returns, properties, stream and sink items), visible in introspection (ww_self::Type::MaxLen), honoured by the dynamic client and Python; raising a bound is compatible, lowering or adding one breaking (ww api check). SerializeShrinkWrap::MAX_SIZE: Option<MaxSize>, the worst-case size of a type whose every part is bounded, feeds API-18. docs/types.md, docs/evolution/rules.md, shrink_wrap/tests/max_len.rs, tests/bounded, examples_mcu/mcu_qemu (qemu-bounded).
  • ✅ SW-15 Handle end of buffer when reading evolved fields: a field with #[default = ..] reads as its default only when it starts at the end of the data and runs out of it (Error::is_read_eob); a truncated or malformed value is an error. The flag of an evolved Option / Result falls back with it, #[default] works on any type and its value is used (an Option was always None). Same in the ww_self dynamic decoder. Padding bits of the old data's last byte read as 0, so bit-sized fields default to their zero value. Decided: no implicit defaults for Vec/String/Option fields without #[default], the attribute is what marks a field as added later (and what ww api check looks for). docs/serdes/derive.md#evolving-types, shrink_wrap/tests/evolution.rs.
  • ✅ SW-16 FutureVersion enum variant: an enum ending with #[future_version] Unknown(u32) reads an unknown discriminant into it instead of failing with EnumFutureVersionOrMalformedData, and writes it back; an Unsized enum skips the newer variant's fields with its size slot, sized / self_describing ones only survive new unit variants. No wire number of its own, no change to ELEMENT_SIZE, left out of the API model. The ww_self dynamic decoder reads an unknown variant of an Unsized enum as <unknown N>. Added by default since SW-47. docs/serdes/derive.md#enum-variants-from-a-newer-version, shrink_wrap/tests/evolution.rs.
  • ✅ SW-48 Bit-sized fields and variant payloads: U1..U64 / I2..I64 (u7, ub10, i2.. in the API model) as struct fields, enum variant payloads and #[ww_trait] method arguments, returns and properties, packed bit after bit with a sub-byte discriminant: enum I2cAddress { Seven(U7), Ten(U10) } with ww_repr = u1, self_describing takes 8 or 11 bits instead of 16 or 24 with u8 / u16. Server and client codegen (it panicked on such a method argument), I16 (was missing), From / TryFrom to and from the backing integer. The dynamic client and Python already handled them, now tested byte for byte against derived types; the C runtime has the bit reads. Same wire format (shrink_wrap/tests/sub_byte.rs, tests/dynamic, tests/methods, docs/serdes/showcase.md#bit-sized-fields-and-variant-payloads-a-7-or-10-bit-i2c-address).
  • ✅ SW-47 #[future_version] variant by default: the derive adds Unknown(u32) to every Unsized enum with a free discriminant; no_future_version opts out (framework enums whose readers must fail: ww_self model, MultiIndex), future_version = Name renames it, final_structure / self_describing / sized enums only get it when written. A Rust API change of every such enum (exhaustive matches need the arm), not of the wire or the API model. docs/serdes/derive.md#enum-variants-from-a-newer-version, shrink_wrap/tests/evolution.rs.
  • 📋 SW-17 Const / magic type · v0.5 — a simple type with a generic parameter that serializes a constant value or byte string and checks it on deserialization, failing on a mismatch. For example the magic field in ww_self (a plain u32 today).
  • ✅ SW-18 Size-of-enclosing-type field TailSize<N>: a field the derive macro fills in with the size of the rest of the value once it is serialized (a UVlq32 right-justified in N bytes, 1 to 5), in any position, nested types each with their own. Readers bound the value by it (a longer buffer stops at the right byte, a truncated one errors, newer trailing fields are skipped) or skip it without parsing. Fields before it must be Sized or SelfDescribing, checked at compile time. docs/serdes/shrink_wrap.md, showcase.
  • 📋 SW-42 MAX_SIZE on owned types · v0.5.x — SerializeShrinkWrapOwned has no worst-case size yet, only the borrowed trait has (SW-19); host code sizing a buffer for an owned value uses the borrowed type's.
  • 📋 SW-20 Sub-type numbers · v0.5.x — numbers restricted to a range, like 10..=25, or a set with gaps, like 0..=8, 12, 16; checked on serialization and deserialization, possibly using fewer bits on the wire (docs/types.md, "Subtypes").
  • 📋 SW-21 Multi-dimensional arrays (2D, 3D).
  • 🚧 SW-22 Fuzz shrink_wrap — fuzz/ has one shrink_wrap target, shrink-wrap-tail-size (TailSize types round-tripped, random bytes into their readers); shrink-wrap-series (SW-31, SW-32) and shrink-wrap-ref-vec (SW-37) came with their features, shrink-wrap-option-any-vec with SW-55 and DER-13 (sparse structs). Round-trip every built-in type and the derive's features.
  • 🔍 SW-23 Tuple enum variants evolution — check that tuple variants evolve as docs/evolution/rules.md says (fields can be appended) and add a test.
  • 💡 SW-24 ZigZag encoding for signed variable length numbers — consider ZigZag (as in protobuf) so that small negative values stay short, e.g. signed counterparts of UNib32/UVlq32.
  • 💡 SW-25 In-place builder for server handlers · v0.5.x — a new step-by-step / partial builder (e.g. for a RefVec) might be useful with the new Context in server handlers, to write replies and events straight into the buffer. It might not work out.
  • 💡 SW-26 Map support — HashMap/BTreeMap, probably as a Vec of (K, V).
  • 💡 SW-27 In-place editing of serialized data.
  • 🚧 SW-28 Compression wrappers · v0.5.x — the time-series part is done as SW-31 (Delta, DeltaOfDelta) and SW-32 (XorFloat); in-place dictionary compression as Compression<T> (strings?) stays an idea.
  • 💡 SW-29 Flatten support — apply a type's layout across struct/enum boundaries.
  • 💡 SW-30 derive_shrink_wrap on a whole module at once. For definitions in separate files with own syntax, see standalone definition files.
  • 💡 SW-56 Tri-state slots in OptionAnyVec — absent / value / error per slot, e.g. a property update that says why one value is missing. The header has room for it: mode nibbles 4..=15 are reserved (a reader fails on them today), so 2-valued vecs don't pay for it.
  • ✅ DER-1 #[derive_shrink_wrap(..)] attribute with clear syntax, no hidden magic and good error messages (docs/serdes/derive.md); replaced #[derive(ShrinkWrap)].
  • ✅ DER-2 Discriminant checks: discriminants must fit ww_repr, implicit ones are numbered like in Rust.
  • ✅ DER-3 #[default = ..] for evolved fields and #[flag] relocation.
  • ✅ DER-4 TailBytes must be last: rejected anywhere but as the last field of a struct or enum variant, and nested in Option, Vec, tuples or arrays (check_tail_bytes_position), like UVlq32Backfill must be first.
  • ✅ DER-10 Generic arguments on user field types: Foo<u8>, Wrapper<'i, T> are emitted as written, Wrapper<'i, T> maps to WrapperOwned<T> in the owned variant (docs/serdes/derive.md, type mapping; test shrink_wrap/tests/generic_external.rs).
  • ✅ DER-11 Field type from a macro_rules $T:ty fragment: accepted like the type written directly, instead of rejected as an unsupported syn::Type::Group (test shrink_wrap/tests/macro_ty_fragment.rs).
  • ✅ DER-12 Display from doc comments: a display directive writes core::fmt::Display and core::error::Error (borrowed and owned) from the first doc line of each variant/struct, {field} filled in, #[display("..")] to override; a variant with neither is a compile error. Error enums need no hand-written Display on hosts (docs/serdes/derive.md; test shrink_wrap/tests/display.rs).
  • ✅ DER-13 Sparse structs: #[derive_shrink_wrap(sparse, ..)] on a struct of Option<T> fields (borrowed and owned) encodes it as an OptionAnyVec (SW-55), one slot per field in declaration order or at #[slot = N] (increasing, gaps allowed, a present value in a gap is Error::OptionAnyVecUnknownSlot); a nested sparse struct is one slot. Fields are only appended. A non-Option field or a combination with final_structure / sized / self_describing / fixed_layout / head_tail is a compile error. For the per trait level <Level>Update of SRV-18 (docs/serdes/derive.md, docs/evolution/rules.md; test shrink_wrap/tests/sparse.rs, fuzz shrink-wrap-option-any-vec). API types may use it, but ww_self has no sparse struct yet: introspection describes one as a plain struct of Options, so dynamic clients decode it wrong until TOOL-11.
  • 📋 DER-5 #[since = "x.y.z"] on fields — generate correct evolution code from it (TODO in shrink_wrap_derive/src/lib.rs).
  • 📋 DER-6 Check that TailBytes ends the outer type too — a struct ending in TailBytes used as a non-last field of an outer sized / final_structure type ("last in the first Unsized type on the way up") is not visible to the derive; needs a marker on the type, e.g. an associated const, and a compile-time assertion in the outer type.
  • 📋 DER-7 Prefix enum discriminants · v0.5.x.
  • ✅ DER-8 #[cfg(..)] on enum variants — a variant keeps its discriminant in every configuration, a build without it reads Error::EnumVariantDisabled (docs/serdes/derive.md). First user: ww_numeric::NumericValue, one cargo feature per number type (32 to 8 bytes in RAM with 32-bit types only). Not yet: #[cfg] on fields (it would change the wire format, should be a compile error), ww_si enums.

items.title: API model and codegen (API)
items.text:
• ✅ API-1 Methods, properties, streams and sinks, nested traits (docs/api/overview.md).
  • ✅ API-2 Arrays of resources with ValidIndices and a built-in array size getter returning a range or list.
  • ✅ API-3 Global traits from ww_stdlib (impl Trait) and trait attachments (examples/all_gpio).
  • ✅ API-4 Results: methods return RpcResult (Ready, Defer, Unimplemented), properties return GetResult/SetResult, with user errors and property errors.
  • ✅ API-5 Request Context in every handler: seq, medium, event out, deferred replies.
  • ✅ API-6 Event, EventKind and error builders.
  • ✅ API-7 match on index slices, the base of multi-read support.
  • ✅ API-8 build.rs codegen via gen_server/gen_client, as an alternative to the proc macro.
  • ✅ API-9 Full name chains in generated names (fixed the event_sideband collision).
  • ✅ API-10 Type paths from Cargo: trait source path, external types in API crates as full paths.
  • ✅ API-11 Sync and async servers, async / blocking / promise clients from the same trait.
  • ✅ API-28 Credit-based flow control for sinks — #[credit] sink!(..): the device grants credit in bytes of items (the serialized value of each write, never split; StreamSideband::Credit { have, grant }), so a receive buffer holds as many items as fit whatever their sizes; the host waits when out of credit (async, blocking, try_send), writes carry the byte position of their first byte so a lossy medium resumes with go-back-N from have (Resend, CreditQuery), flush() waits for the final ack. No deadlock: generated <SINK>_MAX_ITEM_BYTES (from MAX_SIZE, MaxLen bounds included) and SinkCredit::sized_for() check at compile time that the buffer holds the largest item and cap the re-grant threshold, the host fails an item bigger than the buffer with StreamError::ItemTooBig. Device state in ww_client_server::credit::SinkCredit, dynamic and Python clients too. Used by ww_dfu StageBulk::plan. For bulk transfers (chunky OTA plans over LTE-M/LoRa/UDP), UART bridges, CAN tx. See also CLT-18 backpressure (docs/api/streams.md, tests/credit_sink).
  • ✅ API-31 Stream functions — #[stream(T, counted)] fn name(args) -> Result<A, E> and #[counted] / #[reliable] stream!(name: T): every stream (plain ones too) is opened by calling it (RequestKind::StreamOpen), with typed arguments and result; the device's handler named like the stream decides, Ok starts a session, close_<name> closes it. Counted and reliable streams keep their state in what stream_<name>() returns (ww_stream::tx::Counted / Reliable), resume by cursor (name_resume(cursor)), answer a read with their StreamStatus (name_status()), send with stream_data_ser().<name>_send (counted) or push into the store with <name>_push (reliable), which the generated poll_streams sends by priority between requests and resends on the host's ResendFrom; ww api scaffold, introspection (ApiItemKind::StreamFn), compatibility check and API diff know them. Includes API-15. Not yet: reliable streams in resource arrays (poll_streams refuses them), the open arguments in StreamStatus, stream functions in the dynamic client and Python (CLT-23), streams that detach by themselves when the link goes down (a resume re-attaches) (docs/api/stream_reliability.md, tests/streams_reliable).
  • ✅ API-16 Optional items — #[optional] / #[optional(group)] on a trait's methods, properties and streams; a server leaves them out with ww_codegen!(.., omit = ["i2c.pullups"]) or omit_if(<cfg>) = [..] (the user crate's features), pays no dispatch arm and writes no handler (about 100 bytes of flash per item on Cortex-M). Only optional items can be left out (compile error otherwise). A call answers Unimplemented from the level's fallback arm (id < ITEM_COUNT), the device's model lists the omitted items (ww_self omitted, root_omitted), so the generated and dynamic clients and Python fail locally with NotImplementedByDevice; ww api scaffold --omit, CLI tree and Python show them (docs/api/optional_items.md, tests/traits). Not yet: #[optional] on ww_impl!, the GUI (wire_weaver_tool).
  • ✅ API-32 Per-method error lists — #[errors(Common(InUse), Nack, ..)] on a trait method, a stream function (the open's Result error) or above a property! with an error type (its reads and writes): checked against the error enum when the trait is parsed (a compile error on a wrong name), in the API model (ww_self Method, StreamFn and Property errors), generated client and rustdoc # Errors with each variant's doc line, ww api tree, Python help(), ww api check (compatible); the generated and dynamic clients warn when a device returns a variant outside the list, tests fail (tests_common). Nothing on the device (docs/api/methods.md#error-lists, tests/methods, tests/properties, tests/streams_reliable). Not yet: the generated client's property reads (their errors are raw bytes, so only the dynamic client checks them); the GUI (wire_weaver_tool).
  • 📋 API-12 Calculate max path depth in server codegen · v0.5 — MAX_DEPTH is hardcoded to 16 in wire_weaver_core/src/codegen/api_server.rs.
  • 📋 API-13 Error system, remove unwraps from codegen · v0.5 — report errors with spans instead of panicking.
  • 📋 API-14 Load API crates from crates.io · v0.5 — the crate walker handles path and workspace dependencies; crate = "version" dependencies hit a todo!() in wire_weaver_core/src/transform/crate_walker.rs. Also dependencies from git (backlog). Every crate downloaded from crates.io has only such dependencies, so until this is done a published API crate whose API uses another crate's types or traits doesn't compile for its users or on docs.rs (DOC-6).
  • 💡 API-33 Narrow error types per method — generated per-method error enums with the crate enum's discriminants, as server handler return types only (narrow_errors = true), for a compile-time contract on the device. Explored and not recommended for clients: friction in every driver crate.
  • ✅ API-35 Stream functions with a borrowed error type · v0.5 — a stream function whose Result error has a lifetime (#[stream(I2cRecord<'i>, counted)] fn records(..) -> Result<(), I2cError<'i>>, every IO family error since it holds CommonError<'i>) compiles on the server with the handler signature ww api scaffold prints (RpcResult<Result<(), I2cError<'_>>>, an error borrowed from the server), for plain, counted and reliable streams, sync and async servers: the generated dispatch takes the Ok value out of the result before it opens the stream's state (tests/streams_borrowed_error). An Ok value that borrows from the server still can't.
  • ✅ API-36 Const items served from a value · v0.5 — a const NAME: T; of a #[ww_trait] is served without a get_<name> handler: the server struct implements the generated <RootTrait>Consts with const NAME: T = ..; (a Rust const) or, picked with const_model = "NAME=fn", fn name(&self) -> T for a value fixed at boot or link time (OTP, chip id, build id); names carry the trait item chain prefix (BOARD_BOARD / board_board). ww api scaffold --const-model prints the impl. Clients read a const once per connection, then answer from a cache (generated, dynamic and Python clients, promises too); ww introspect shows const values (tests/consts, docs/api/properties.md). ww_firmware_info, ww_board_info, ww_uid and ww_user_info servers use it.
  • ✅ API-38 Observe requests · v0.5.x — RequestKind::Observe on a trait level: per property Off, OnChange, Periodic or OnChangeOrBeat and a byte budget, the device answers with what it granted; updates arrive as one EventKind::PropertyUpdate per level carrying any subset of its properties (SW-55). Only +observe properties can be observed. Protocol ww_client_server::observe (docs/std_library/ww_client_server.md), device side SRV-18, host side CLT-28 (docs/api/properties.md#observing-changes, tests/observe).
  • 💡 API-37 Const values in the introspection blob — a codegen option putting the values of const items into the device's introspection data, so ww info gets them with the link setup and no extra reads. Costs flash per device, so not a default.
  • 💡 API-39 Batched property samples — K samples of one fast property in one update, compressed with Delta / XorFloat (SW-50), for values sampled faster than the link can carry one update each.
  • 📋 API-17 Methods arguments to a user struct · v0.5.x.
  • 🚧 API-18 Size analysis · v0.5.x — maximum buffer usage in the worst case, auto-calculated buffer sizes for events, arguments and outputs. Done: MAX_SIZE of types (SW-19) and per-method <METHOD>_REQUEST_MAX_LEN / <METHOD>_RESPONSE_MAX_LEN consts in no_alloc servers, checked at compile time against a buffer in tests/bounded and examples_mcu/mcu_qemu. Missing: consts for properties, streams and sinks, the largest of all of them for a whole API (to size ww_device buffers such as UdpBuffers<MAX_MESSAGE_LEN> automatically), paths of nested traits counted exactly (now the worst case of the full path), the same consts on the client.
  • 📋 API-19 Change dispatcher match order to process common requests faster · v0.5.x.
  • 🚧 API-20 Trait paths on the server side · v0.5 — servers serve PathKind::GlobalFull requests (crate, version and trait name) wherever the trait sits in the tree, ErrorKind::TraitNotFound otherwise (tests/cross_version, docs/api/addressing.md). Missing: PathKind::GlobalCompact (compact ids of traits are not in the API model yet, none is assigned), traits under a resource array.
  • 📋 API-21 no_alloc = false servers — don't compile today.
  • ⛔ API-22 Implement the same trait several times → enum selector · v0.5.x — stalled. At least print a proper error when a trait is implemented twice (tests/traits_api).
  • ⛔ API-23 Index chain array → named arguments · v0.5.x — stalled. Generating ad-hoc structs with named index fields might be a good ergonomic: users see the names through IDE lookup instead of guessing array indices.
  • 📋 API-29 Bounds of resource array indices · v0.5.x — stream!(adc[8]: u16) or motor[1..=4], checked by the server before a handler is called and visible in introspection (docs/api/arrays.md). Lengths of lists and strings inside a resource's type are bounded with MaxLen (SW-19). With a bound, observed properties (SRV-18) can get a table per array element: until then a trait level in a resource array can't be observed (STD-31 ww_gpio pin level waits for it).
  • 🚧 API-30 Counted and reliable streams · v0.5 — counted streams put a head in every event (flags and a length-coded 64-bit pos in units the device names when it sends, the event's units, lost, optional device time t), so drops on the device, link losses and duplicates are reported exactly and item types carry no seq / lost / t fields (IO family D4, D5). Reliable streams add Ack / ResendFrom / Query (go-back-N, grants in bytes), keep unacknowledged events in a store, resume by cursor after a reconnect with the latest values first and the backlog beside them; a send scheduler with priorities between streams; typed cnt counters (docs/api/stream_reliability.md). Done, the protocol core: wire types in ww_client_server::stream (StreamHead with its hand-laid encoding, byte-verified; StreamCursor, StreamOpened, EventKind::StreamItem, RequestKind::StreamOpen, the sideband), the ww_stream crate (Counted, Reliable, Receiver, RamRing, Scheduler, StreamCnt; sans-IO, no_std, tested over a seeded lossy link with random disconnects), ww_self::ApiItemKind::StreamFn, codegen (API-31), the host runtime (CLT-23). Missing: credit sinks on it (API-34). The persistent store is done (SRV-15).
  • 📋 API-34 Credit sinks on the stream protocol · v0.5 — positions in units (64 bit), Ack / Query / Resend shared with reliable streams, sessions and resume for credit sinks, so a DFU plan continues after a reconnect; SinkCredit moves into ww_stream (docs/api/stream_reliability.md).
  • 💡 API-24 Guarded calls for critical resources · v0.5.x — for safety-critical actions, such as starting a motor or switching high power, a request that happens to match predefined bytes must not be enough. Add an extra check, e.g. a CRC over the resource identity and arguments (a "strict mode" per resource), or a request/response challenge before the call is executed.
  • 💡 API-25 Refactor codegen to use an IR · v0.5.x.
  • 🚧 API-26 Generate C · v0.5.x, and an FFI example. The C runtime is there (SW-43 c-runtime); generated .h / .c for an API's types, a device-side dispatcher, introspection as a const blob and ww_framer are not.
  • 💡 API-27 Standalone definition files with custom syntax — APIs and types in their own files, with a friendlier syntax: nested levels, no macro calls, SI units. Tried twice already, approach with care:
  • at the very beginning of this repo, a YAML based language;
  • later, a big effort to support a custom syntax, which turned into a project of its own and took a lot of resources away from the actual work.

Plain Rust with #[ww_trait] and #[derive_shrink_wrap] is the current answer; revisit only with a concrete benefit that outweighs the cost of a parser, tooling and IDE support.

items.title: Server / device side (SRV)
items.text:
• ✅ SRV-1 no_std, no-alloc server, IO-free generated code.
  • ✅ SRV-2 Sans-IO DeviceLink, async Server with wait()/handle() for a user-owned event loop, and blocking::Server.
  • ✅ SRV-3 Fully split TX and RX flows for every transport (fixed the half-duplex interlock), framing without IO.
  • ✅ SRV-4 User handlers called straight from the RX loop, transport glue extracted into ww_device.
  • ✅ SRV-5 Device descriptors: serial, WireWeaver version, API id, version, hash and user label in the USB interface string.
  • ✅ SRV-6 Media: USB (embassy), RTT, WebSocket and UDP (both also on embassy-net).
  • ✅ SRV-7 UDP device medium — ww_device::udp, one frame per datagram over any datagram socket, one host at a time, another host takes over by starting link setup (docs/transport/udp.md).
  • ✅ SRV-15 Stream stores and backfill — ww_stream::store: what a reliable stream (API-30) keeps until the host acknowledges it: RamRing (API-30) and LogStore, a power-cut safe log on a block device (feature log-store; SdMedium on an embedded-sdmmc BlockDevice with sdmmc, NorMedium on an embedded-storage-async NorFlash with nor-flash) that keeps session, positions and clock epochs across reboots; drop-newest or drop-oldest when full, counted exactly. Tested with a power cut at every write (ww_stream/src/tests/log_store.rs); docs/api/stream_stores.md.
  • ✅ SRV-16 Persistent RAM store — ww_stream::store::PersistentRamRing (feature persistent-ram): a reliable stream's store in .uninit RAM that survives a soft reset (fault → reset), for the logs before a crash (STD-26). Header slots and records checked by CRC at boot, so garbage after a power-on is never taken for data; continues session and positions like LogStore, a new clock epoch per boot. Tested with a fault after every byte written (ww_stream/src/tests/persistent_ram.rs); docs/api/stream_stores.md.
  • ✅ SRV-18 Observed properties on the device — servers of APIs with +observe properties answer Observe requests (API-38) and send PropertyUpdates from the generated poll_properties: ObserveState with one table per trait level sized at compile time, a sparse <Trait>Update per level (DER-13), mark_changed_<name>() (called for value_on_changed writes), periodic properties sampled through their getter. A token bucket per level at the granted budget, earliest deadline first, at most one update per level per call, the rest slips and counts as missed; properties have a reserved share of the link (ObserveLimits::total_budget) next to stored streams. Observe is untrusted input: validated in full before anything changes, clamped, bounded work, refused per entry. Levels under a resource array answer OperationNotSupported until their bound is known (API-29), +observe properties in an array or #[optional] aren't observable yet. ww_stream::observe, docs/api/properties.md#observing-changes; tests tests/observe (fake clock, real host event loop), ww_stream/src/observe/tests.rs.
  • ⛔ SRV-8 One crate per role for firmware and host · v0.5 — blocked on generated code using absolute paths. Agreed direction, instead of putting everything into wire_weaver behind features or splitting by std/no_std:
  • wire_weaver stays lean (shrink_wrap, macros, ww_version, result types) since every API crate and ww_stdlib crate depends on it;
  • ww_device re-exports wire_weaver, ww_framer, ww_link and gets features usb-embassy, rtt, udp, ws, defmt, embassy-time, std;
  • wire_weaver_client re-exports wire_weaver with transport features.

Requires: codegen emitting paths through the role crate (or a crate = ".." argument / proc-macro-crate; WIRE_WEAVER_REEXPORTS in the crate walker is partly there), and wire_weaver_usb_embassy building in the root workspace or merging into ww_device. Separately consider making wire_weaver's std default off.

  • 📋 SRV-9 Handle USB suspend/resume · v0.5 — run until suspend, wait for resume, loop (mcu/wire_weaver_usb_embassy). Later (v0.5.x): detect the host going to sleep and keep the connection, informing the device.
  • 📋 SRV-10 Collect error codes into an ELF section for easier error decoding · v0.5.x.
  • 📋 SRV-11 Link statistics in ww_device (TODO in link.rs).
  • 💡 SRV-12 std server on Tower · v0.5.
  • 💡 SRV-13 IPC over USB / multi-app devices / USB multiplexer · v0.5.x.
  • 💡 SRV-14 FPGA server · v0.5.x.

items.title: Client / host side (CLT)
items.text:
• ✅ CLT-1 std client with async, blocking and promise flavors, prepared call objects, no root() needed.
  • ✅ CLT-2 Generic sans-IO event loop over a Transport, independent TX and RX flows.
  • ✅ CLT-3 USB transport on nusb: endpoint addresses from descriptors, bulk with lower priority, vec recycling.
  • ✅ CLT-4 RTT transport over a debug probe, control block address from an ELF file.
  • ✅ CLT-5 WebSocket, UDP and in-process transports.
  • ✅ CLT-6 DynClient and dynamic resources, for APIs known only at runtime.
  • ✅ CLT-7 Introspection cache keyed by API hash with and without docs, with a download timeout.
  • ✅ CLT-8 Compatibility check on connect: each resource is checked against device introspection when the API hash differs.
  • ✅ CLT-9 Connection selectors, clear errors when no device is found, disconnect() releases the transport.
  • ✅ CLT-24 One ? per call — a method returning Result<T, E> gives Result<T, CallError<E>> (Device(E), Unimplemented { resource } or Client(Error)) from call, blocking_call and promises, a property with a user error type the same from write and write_promise, instead of Result<Result<T, E>, Error> and ??; Error::is_unimplemented() for items without an error type (docs/api/methods.md#client-side, tests/methods).
  • ✅ CLT-25 ww info and ww report · v0.5 — ww info shows firmware, board, ids, label and last reset of any device by global trait path, whatever its API version; ww report adds the counters, the stored defmt log and the crash's addresses named with the ELF, found by build id, as one file a tester sends; ww elf add <elf|archive> fills the ELF directory from an ELF or a release's <firmware>-<version>-elf.tar.zst (shared with cnt elf add, cnt_core::elf). Library crate ww_report (Contract, collect_info, collect_report), docs/std_library/device_contract.md, tests/device_report. The stored log is a stream and streams open on the absolute path only (CLT-23), so ww report reads the device's introspection data for the log's path; ww info needs none. Not yet: fetching the release archive by itself.
  • ✅ CLT-28 Observing properties on the host · v0.5.x — generated std clients have observe(cfg) per trait level with +observe properties (an Observer of the level's <Trait>Update) and observe_<name>(mode) per property, fanned out from the level: one device subscription per level covering all its observers (merged modes, biggest budget), sent again when an observer comes, changes (configure) or goes, Off after the last one; <Trait>Observe typed settings and what was granted, <Trait>Latest latest-value cache with receive times; subscriptions sent again by resume_streams() after a reconnect; Error::Unsupported for a device whose API model predates API-38 (wire_weaver_client::observe, docs/api/properties.md#observing, tests/observe, observe_e2e_tests). Not yet: levels under a resource array, the dynamic client and Python (TOOL-11).
  • 🚧 CLT-10 Trait calls that work on any device · v0.5 — serial, user label, a CLI that works with all devices. ww list with filters and USB interface string metadata are done, and global trait calls on any device whatever its API version: ClientConfig::traits_only(), DynClient::global_attachment() (served through API-20, tests/cross_version), ww dfu reboot, ww counters (STD-25) and ww info / ww report (CLT-25). Missing: CLI commands for the other ww_stdlib traits (GPIO, UART, ...).
  • 📋 CLT-11 Typed property handles · v0.5 — RwProperty/RoProperty/WoProperty so that .prop_name().read(), .prepare_write(1).blocking(), .asynch().await work.
  • 📋 CLT-12 Stream receive timeout · v0.5 — and a beat timeout between updates.
  • 🔍 CLT-13 Typed attachments with TraitMarker · v0.5 — trait attachments exist (Attachment, examples/all_gpio); check whether a typed marker is still wanted.
  • 💡 CLT-14 no_std client (client = "raw") — documented as not working in ClientModel::Raw, its test is commented out in tests/traits. Its generated code serializes arguments into a fixed 128 byte scratch and then calls .to_vec(), which isn't no_std; it should write into a caller-provided buffer instead. The std clients (std_client, trait_client) already serialize with to_ww_bytes_owned() and have no size limit.
  • ✅ CLT-15 Multi read/write/call · v0.5.x — servers with multi_req = true dispatch MultiRead, MultiCall and MultiWrite (Same or Different args), each index answered on its own (Either<Error, value>), and answer malformed multi requests with errors instead of panicking (tests/multi_req). Client side: generic MultiRead/ MultiCall/MultiWrite tuple traits (any arity 2..=8, any depth, not just root 2-tuples), read_array/ call_array/write_array for homogeneous requests across an array's indices (List/Range/Mask32, Same or Different args chosen automatically), and a DynResource equivalent for the dynamic client (tests/properties, tests/methods, tests/dynamic). Deferred methods inside a multi request are refused with OperationNotSupported.
  • 📋 CLT-16 Verify the hash of a cached API bundle · v0.5.x (wire_weaver_client/src/local_registry.rs).
  • 📋 CLT-17 Reliable requests over unreliable media · v0.5.x — a second, non-increasing seq number to guard against a lost reply for a request that was executed, when executing twice is not OK. Relevant for UDP.
  • 🔍 CLT-18 Backpressure — commands already go through a bounded channel (ClientConfig::cmd_queue_size), so user code should block or yield when the queue is full; add tests for it. A request sent while every request id is in flight waits for one. Flow control towards the device for sinks: API-28 credit-sinks.
  • 📋 CLT-19 Connection priority in the client config (TODO in config.rs).
  • 📋 CLT-20 Bound check of generated byte sink writes · v0.5.x — a sink!(x: MaxLen<RefVec<'i, u8>, N>) write from a generated client is sent as raw bytes without a length check, the device rejects a longer one (ArgsDesFailed); the dynamic client and Python already check before sending.
  • 🚧 CLT-21 Follow a device across a reboot into other firmware — for DFU (ww_dfu BootControl::reboot(Updater)): reconnect to the same device by serial number, whatever answers there, with a timeout. Done for USB: wire_weaver_client::follow (Follow, Bus, Found), and the RP2350 / RP2040 boot ROM as the updater: ww_picoboot (PICOBOOT host on nusb, SimRp2350 for tests), follow::rp2_update(), ww bootsel, tested end to end on a simulated device (tests/follow_reboot, docs/transport/follow_reboot.md). The PICOBOOT host moved to its own repo, picoboot_host (evaluated the crates.io picoboot 0.3.0 crate first: no sans-IO boundary to put SimRp2350 behind, no Image/UF2 handling, no orchestrated flash+verify, no chip_id/GET_INFO — adopting it would have meant donating most of ww_picoboot upstream anyway); wire_weaver depends on it as ww_picoboot (a git dependency on github.com/vhrdtech/picoboot_host until it is on crates.io). wire_weaver_client's picoboot feature (off by default) gates follow::rp2_update() and the ww_picoboot re-export, so a host app that only talks WireWeaver over USB doesn't pull in PICOBOOT; ww bootsel turns it on, and follow::rp2_update_with() (what tests/follow_reboot runs against a simulated device) needs neither it nor usb. Missing: a run against a Pico 2 / rePort; RTT (another control block: a second ELF or a RAM scan) and UDP / WebSocket (the port may change); asking for the reboot from the CLI needs CLT-10.
  • 📋 CLT-22 One Sink::send for borrowed and owned items — owned types (FooOwned) implement only SerializeShrinkWrapOwned, so they go through send_owned; one send for both (a sink item trait, or the derive implementing both), then drop send_owned.
  • 🚧 CLT-23 Stream positions, gaps and resume on the host · v0.5 — Commander::prepare_stream_open / prepare_stream_resume (what generated code calls, PreparedStreamOpen, StreamOpenResult), PositionedStream with StreamEvent::Item / Gap / Resumed / BackfillDone / Disconnected, live and backfill runs and split(), StreamStats, AckMode::OnReceive / Explicit, cursors; every stream's queue is bounded (ClientConfig::stream_queue_bytes, plain streams report RawStreamEvent::Dropped); after disconnect().keep_streams() streams wait and Commander::resume_streams() resumes them; DynPositionedStream and the Python PositionedStream (docs/api/stream_reliability.md, docs/python.md). Tested end to end against a hand-written device: S4 host stuck, S6 host restart, resume after a reconnect (wire_weaver_client/src/event_loop/stream_e2e_tests.rs). Generated clients open streams through it (tests/streams_reliable, API-31); the dynamic client and Python pass the stream function's arguments and return its result. Missing: counted and reliable streams on trait paths (events carry the absolute path), the reconnect itself (EX-10), lossy-medium scenarios (TEST-19).

items.title: Transports and protocols (TR)
items.text:
• ✅ TR-1 ww_framer: packs many small messages into one packet or splits a big one across packets; U2Head with 1 byte overhead, CRC, recovery from missed frames, fuzzed.
  • ✅ TR-2 ww_link: link setup, device info, API version exchange.
  • ✅ TR-3 USB, RTT, WebSocket, UDP and in-process (messages, or simulated USB: real USB framing and packet sizes, in_process::usb_device).
  • ✅ TR-4 USB CDC-NCM: WebSocket over a USB network adapter, with a DHCP server so the host gets an address by itself, ping and a hello page over HTTP (examples_mcu/rp2, ww_ws_ncm); UDP the same way (ww_udp_ncm).
  • 💡 TR-5 USB CDC-NCM extras — test on Windows, macOS, iOS and Android; serve files from an SD card over HTTP; mass storage with a README.
  • 📋 TR-6 CAN · v0.5.x — server and client, using CANopen (docs/transport/overview.md).
  • 📋 TR-7 UART · v0.5.x.
  • 💡 TR-8 IP / WireGuard · v0.5.x.
  • 💡 TR-9 EtherCAT.
  • 💡 TR-10 One-shot connect — no link setup at all: the host sends the API hash and its requests in one go; when the hash matches, the device runs them right away, else it answers with its hash and drops them and the normal setup follows. With message aggregation both arrive in one packet or frame, so a request over LoRa or LTE-M costs no extra round trip (introspection skipped by hash, CLT-7). Open: replayed and duplicate packets (CLT-17), which requests may run unannounced, how the hash is versioned. Needed by ww_dfu updates over slow links.
  • 💡 TR-11 MQTT / store-and-forward transport — devices offline most of the time pick up a retained message on wake (an update plan, config), replies queued on the broker. Look at MQTT-SN and LwM2M first.
  • 🚧 TR-12 USB throughput on small MCUs — measured with ww usb-loopback on Donguru (STM32G0B1, Cortex-M0+ 64 MHz, USB FS behind the board's HS hub, 15 Oct 2026). Done: U2Head encodes and decodes whole bytes in u32 instead of bit by bit (ww_framer framed.rs, was ~15% of the device's CPU per packet); the async device server flushes replies at once when no other request waits instead of after the accumulation window (ww_device Server::handle; DFU transcripts +1-2 packets). WireWeaverClass::with_endpoints() lets firmware allocate the endpoints, e.g. double-buffered bulk ones (Donguru, embassy-rs/embassy#7275: raw bulk 500 -> 950 kB/s OUT on the G0). Next: CRC through a pluggable checksum so MCUs can use their CRC unit (~13% of the CPU per packet on the M0+); a host-side flush for lone requests that keeps packetization deterministic (flushing whenever the event loop goes idle made the DFU transcripts vary between runs); the same reply flush for the blocking server.

items.title: Introspection (ww_self, INT)
items.text:
• ✅ INT-1 API model AST with syn-style Visit/VisitMut, sent by devices as introspection data.
  • ✅ INT-2 Bundles recording crate versions, signatures of skipped traits and types.
  • ✅ INT-3 Relocated #[flag] fields in introspection data and dynamic serialization.
  • 📋 INT-4 Bit-aligned integers in ww_self · v0.5 — un/in types (u1..u32, nibbles) are not supported in the introspection model yet, so the dynamic client and Python can't handle them. Add them, with tests through dynamic serdes.
  • 📋 INT-5 Documentation pass on ww_self · v0.5 — doc comments are missing (TODO in ww_self/src/lib.rs).
  • 📋 INT-6 sized / final_structure on ww_self types · v0.5 — where a type is unlikely to evolve, to make introspection data smaller. Can't be undone later, so decide per type.
  • 💡 INT-7 Compress ww_self strings with a pre-shared dictionary — partly addressed by leaving snapshot-known traits and types out of introspection data.
  • 💡 INT-8 Model enums that tolerate newer variants — the ww_self enums (Type, ApiItemKind, Fields, ...) and ww_numeric::NumericAnyType are no_future_version (SW-47): a host reading a newer model fails as a whole. With Unknown handled in every walker (visitor, signature, inline, values, compat, CLI, Python), an older host could show the rest of a newer device's API and mark the unknown parts.

items.text:

  • 💡 EVO-7 Git dirty flag — not implemented, although the old tracker had it as done: neither ww_version nor codegen record git state. Uncommitted API changes are still caught, since they change the API's SHA signature. Firmware git info (sha, dirty, branch, tag) can be exposed through ww_firmware_info's bedrock_build_info stream. Decide whether the link or version also needs it.
  • 📋 EVO-8 Snapshots of crates.io crates — depends on "Load API crates from crates.io" above.

items.title: Standard library (ww_stdlib, STD)
items.text:
• ✅ STD-1 ww_client_server — the request/event model, pruned of sideband/subscribe/rate, variable length seq numbers.
  • ✅ STD-2 ww_version.
  • ✅ STD-3 ww_si and ww_numeric.
  • ✅ STD-4 ww_date_time.
  • ✅ STD-5 ww_gpio.
  • ✅ STD-16 Common errors — ww_error::CommonError (Unsupported, InvalidArgument, InUse, Busy, WrongState, NoPower, Refused, Timeout, Fault, bounded strings), re-exported as wire_weaver::prelude::CommonError, nested first in an error enum as #[common] Common(CommonError) (the derive adds From<CommonError> and HasCommon); recognised by tools by its type (ww_self::TypeOwned::is_common_error): Python RemoteError.common with the doc line as the message, ww api tree -t marks it. Display by hand until DER-12 takes over. Every ww_stdlib API crate with fallible methods uses it except ww_dfu (its Error has no lifetime and predates this; only Unsupported/Busy would map cleanly, left as a follow-up) and ww_can_bus (not ready yet); ww_client_server's ErrorKind is a framework/link-level error, not an API error, so it is out of scope. docs/std_library/ww_error.md, tests/common_error.
  • ✅ STD-19 ww_pwm — Pwm / PwmChannel outputs (set_output, set_duty, stop, state), PwmCapture / PwmCaptureChannel measurements (frequency, duty, pulse width, edge count) over a plain stream with sideband Open / Close. Full rustdoc, mock server and in-process tests (tests/io_pwm), docs page (docs/std_library/ww_pwm.md) (STD-13).
  • ✅ STD-17 ww_timebase — Clock: device time as ww_si::Second (full width via now(), truncated elsewhere), sync master / slave (IRIG-B, PPS), sync_status, a time_map stream mapping device time to shared time, set_time_of_day for a master. tests/io_timebase, docs/std_library/ww_timebase.md.
  • ✅ STD-18 ww_adc — Adc, AdcStream (sideband Open / Close), AdcCapture. Fill-in done: full rustdoc, tests/io_adc mock server (one test per trait), docs/std_library/ww_adc.md, API snapshot (STD-13).
  • ✅ STD-20 ww_onewire — OneWire: addressed transactions with strong pull-up, reset, paged and bit-level (triplet) ROM search, the real Dallas/Maxim search algorithm. Full rustdoc, docs page (docs/std_library/ww_onewire.md), API snapshot, in-process test with a mock bus (tests/io_onewire).
  • ✅ STD-23 ww_si / ww_numeric extended · v0.5 — quantity groups and host helpers as cargo features, Second as a device timestamp (wrap rule, host Unwrapper), constructors, conversions and comparisons across prefixes and storage, UVlq32 / UVlq64 storage, Baud for baud rates (STD-13). docs/std_library/ww_si.md, docs/std_library/ww_numeric.md. Zero-overhead typed quantities (Volt<u16, Milli>) are not part of it.
  • ✅ STD-24 ww_firmware_info / ww_board_info / ww_uid / ww_user_info device contract · v0.5 — the info crates every device implements. FirmwareInfo const items FIRMWARE (name, version, git, build time, profile), BUILD_ID (GNU build id, finds the ELF) and optional BUILD_RECORD; build::emit() + firmware_summary!() for build.rs, build_id() reader; LastReset (ResetRecord with a Fault per architecture behind cortex-m / riscv, stack words, boot_count, clear). BoardInfo::BOARD with RevisionSource. Uid::IDS, first id is the primary one (USB serial). UserInfo with bounded name / optional notes, UserInfoError, CAPABILITIES and the persistence rule. Docs docs/std_library/ww_{firmware_info,board_info,uid,user_info}.md, tests tests/{firmware_info,board_info,uid,user_info}. The const items are served by get_ handlers until constant items come from the introspection data; properties cannot carry #[errors] yet.
  • 🧪 STD-26 ww_log defmt over reliable streams · v0.5 — ww_log_bare_metal renamed ww_log. LogDefmt { const DEFMT (encoding, build id); frames() }: a reliable stream whose unit is one defmt frame, whole frames per item (up to 512 B), so lost is the exact number of dropped messages and logs from before the host connects arrive by resuming the device's session. LogText { records(); rw level: LevelFilter } with bounded LogRecord, Severity without User, LogError on CommonError. Device side: new crate ww_defmt_logger (global_logger!, lock-free ring with whole-frame commits, RTT tee, pump() into the store, drops reported in place), ring stress-tested on the host with concurrent producers. tests/log_defmt decodes with defmt-decoder end to end; examples/defmt_log (host) and examples_mcu/rp2's rp2_usb_log (USB and RTT at once, build id in flash). docs/std_library/ww_log.md. Hardware check open (no Pico 2 probe on the mesh): just run rp2 usb_log, then examples/defmt_log: logs over USB and RTT at once, lost exact under --flood, logs from before connecting. ww log in the CLI is a later item.
  • ✅ STD-25 ww_counters on cnt words · v0.5 — the device's cnt counters as raw buffer words, decoded on the host with the firmware's ELF found by its build id: Counters::INFO (format, used/capacity words of RAM and backup, build id), read(buffer, offset) pages of UVlq32, reset, optional watch stream (not served by anything yet); read_words / reset_words serve cnt buffers, feature host has WwSource (a cnt_core::Source). ww counters read|watch|tui|reset|info shows the cnt_view views (CLT-10). In the cnt repo: cnt::ram_used_words(), word sources and ELF lookup by build id in cnt_core, cnt_view, and the probe path checks the build id too. Docs docs/std_library/ww_counters.md, tests tests/counters; cnt_core / cnt_view 0.5 from crates.io.
  • ✅ STD-27 reset-record-age · v0.5 — ww_firmware_info::ResetRecord::boots_since_crash: boots since the crash data was saved (0 = the last reset was the crash), so a record kept across later normal resets shows how old it is. bedrock_crash counts it (Crash::boots_since) and the firmware template fills it.
  • ✅ STD-28 ww_indication lightweight rework — cut to one required item: mode: Mode (AllOff / OnlyEssential / Normal). brightness: Brightness (5 levels, one setting for all indicators), identify(duration) (blink everything to find the unit on a bench, errors on CommonError) and NAMES (indicator names, API-36) are each their own #[optional] item. Dropped alert_brightness / AlertBrightness, animation_enable, test_mode / TestMode and HAS_NOT_CONTROLLABLE. Docs docs/std_library/ww_indication.md, tests tests/indication (mock servers with only mode, and with every optional item).
  • ✅ STD-29 ww_can_bus on the stdlib idioms — from simple bridges to bus debuggers. Can is one controller: six required items (capabilities(), configure(CanConfig) answering what was set, config(), the observable status, the counted rx stream, the tx credit sink) and #[optional] set_mode (incl. Config and Sleep), recover, tx_abort, tx_events (marker, measured queue time), bus_errors, protocol_status, bus_load, detect_timing, set_filters, set_layout, rx_buffer, tx_buffer (once or cyclic), transceiver (standby / silent / sleep, wiring faults), terminator, test_pins. CanGroup (interface[]: Can, enable / disable, optional clock source and frequency, performance) for controllers sharing clock, power and message RAM; CanTimeTriggered (TTCAN); CanXl behind the xl feature. Errors on CommonError + OutOfFilters, OutOfMemory, BusOff; defmt no longer pulls std. Docs docs/std_library/ww_can_bus.md, tests tests/io_can (full and minimal node), tests/io_can_group (group, TTCAN, XL).
  • ✅ STD-30 ww_gpio port access — Bank::read_inputs(pins) answers the input levels of the listed pins (indices into pin[]) in the same order, Bank::write_outputs(levels) sets a list of PinLevel { pin, level }, all or nothing; both at one instant where the hardware allows (one register read / write), which BankCapabilities::simultaneous_read / simultaneous_write say, pin by pin in list order otherwise. For bit-banged parallel buses and strobes from the host, which multi-call can't make simultaneous. Pins by index, no masks on the wire (IO family D9). Bank indices 1 and 2 from its reserved range, capabilities appended with #[default = false]. Docs docs/std_library/ww_gpio.md#port-access, tests tests/io_gpio, STM32 boards in examples_mcu (IDR / BSRR).
  • 🚧 STD-6 ww_gpio_hl — usable, some APIs are still missing.
  • 🔍 STD-7 Interrupt left enabled in ww_gpio_hl · v0.5 — the falling edge helper documents that it leaves interrupts enabled; decide whether that is the intended fix or a bug.
  • 🚧 STD-8 Prototypes, to be completed later: ww_i2c, ww_uart, ww_memory (was ww_ll: one word type per trait, optional watches, errors on CommonError, docs page), Known gaps are TODOs in their sources (e.g. SMBus and 7-bit addresses in ww_i2c; ww_can_bus is done in STD-29). ww_log (was ww_log_bare_metal) left for STD-26.
  • 💡 STD-9 Stubs, for later: ww_spi (ww_board_info, ww_firmware_info, ww_user_info and ww_uid moved to STD-24).
  • 🚧 STD-12 ww_dfu firmware update API — traits UpdateNode, BootControl, Inventory, Stage, StageBulk: each node (app, bootloader, recovery app) implements what it needs; A/B live, in place from a stored plan, in place live; step by step or bulk. Carries the octet records of the chunky protocol spec (P2625). End to end test tests/dfu. Guide with the eight update scenarios (2C-APP-STEP Swap Shuttle .. 1L-UPD-BULK Pit-stop Freight), each tested end to end over USB (simulated), WebSocket or UDP with reboots and power cuts, its exchange recorded as a golden transcript the docs include (docs/std_library/ww_dfu.md, tests/dfu_scenarios, just dfu-transcripts). StageBulk::plan is a credit sink (API-28 credit-sinks). Every variable-size field is bounded (SW-19: MAX_PIECE_LEN, MAX_HEADER_LEN, MAX_CHUNKS_PAGE, MAX_PRODUCT_LEN), so every method has a known largest request and reply. Profile::AB(SlotSwitch::{Copy, Remap}) / InPlace. Next: a chunky implementation (chunky NET-1).
  • 🚧 STD-13 IO trait family · v0.5 — ww_gpio, ww_uart (optional Uart::monitor), ww_i2c (+ I2cWatch, I2cMonitor, 10-bit addresses), ww_spi (optional Spi::monitor), ww_adc (STD-18), ww_pwm (STD-19), ww_onewire (STD-20), ww_timebase (STD-17), ww_logic_analyzer / ww_signal_generator (STD-21, STD-22); ww_si values and timestamps (STD-23): frequencies Hertz, baud rates Baud. Family overview in docs/std_library/io_family.md; every crate filled in with full rustdoc, a mock-server test pair tests/io_<x> and a docs page docs/std_library/ww_<x>.md; examples_mcu GPIO and UART boards follow. A bus or bank is configured with one configure(XConfig) answering what was actually set, the IO level inside it (io_level: Option<Volt>, capabilities io_levels / io_level_min / io_level_max). Every crate's error enum starts with #[common] Common(CommonError) (STD-16) and keeps only what is specific (Nack, NoPresence, NoSuchChannel, ...), methods list their variants with #[errors(..)] (API-32). Streams with a configuration are counted stream functions (API-31: AdcStream::samples, LogicStream::data, Pin::event, PwmCaptureChannel::capture, Spi::monitor, I2cMonitor::records, Uart::monitor), Uart::rx and I2cWatch::changes are counted: positions, device losses and the time of the first unit in the event head; UART chunks end on line idle (UartConfig::idle_chars, one back-to-back burst each) and carry the time of their last byte when the device measures it (RxChunk::end). Clients take one ? per call (CLT-24 CallError), Unsized enums read newer variants as Unknown(u32) (SW-47). Review round 1 (15 Oct 2026) done. Open: *_hl crates are STD-14.
  • 🚧 STD-21 ww_logic_analyzer · v0.5.x — LogicAnalyzer (triggered capture into RAM), LogicStream; Raw and per-channel Transitions encodings (SW-31 DeltaOfDelta), staged pattern triggers and protocol stages (UART byte, I2C address, SPI first byte). Skeleton written, transitions as DeltaOfDelta (SW-50), docs page docs/std_library/ww_logic_analyzer.md; mock-server test pair still open (STD-13).
  • 🚧 STD-22 ww_signal_generator · v0.5.x — PatternGenerator (digital, replays analyzer captures through a credit sink), WaveformGenerator (DAC channels). Skeleton written, docs page docs/std_library/ww_signal_generator.md; mock-server test pair still open (STD-13).
  • ⛔ STD-31 Observable ww_gpio pin level · v0.5.x — property!(ro+observe level: Level) on Pin at one of its reserved indices 4..=6, so a host sees input changes without opening the event stream of every pin (slow inputs, a dashboard). Blocked on API-29 array-index-bounds: Pin sits in Bank::pin[] (and banks usually in an array too), and levels under a resource array can't be observed until their bound is known (SRV-18).
  • 💡 STD-10 Device state machine trait like CANopen.
  • 💡 STD-11 Register description registry — WireWeaver for describing device registers.

items.title: Python
items.text:
The wire_weaver Python module talks to any WireWeaver device without generated code. The API tree (traits, methods, properties, streams) is built at runtime from the introspection data the device sends, or from the API crate source. Values are converted to and from plain Python objects and serialized exactly as the generated Rust clients do it, the module is a thin wrapper around the dynamic client in wire_weaver_client.

It is meant for debugging, quick tests and scripts: connect, look at what the device offers, call it. For a typed Python package wrapping one specific API, see the blinky_py example instead (Examples), it wraps the generated Rust client.

Both transports are built in: USB and RTT over a debug probe (probe-rs). Everything is pure Rust, the wheel needs no system libraries.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
The module is built with maturin, from a checkout of the repository (a Rust toolchain is needed):

cd wire_weaver_py
uvx maturin build --release        # wheel in target/wheels/, pip install it anywhere
uvx maturin develop --release      # or install into the active virtual environment

--no-default-features leaves RTT out for a smaller wheel.

Linux permissions

Listing devices works without any setup, but opening one needs read/write access to /dev/bus/usb/..., usually granted to your user with a udev rule. See USB.

items.title: Interactive console
items.text:
From the repository root, just py builds the module into wire_weaver_py/.venv (only when Rust sources changed) and opens a Python prompt with ww imported and the device connected as dev, if exactly one is found or a filter is given:

just py                                        # the only connected USB device
just py --serial 0123 --timeout 5              # pick one: --serial, --label, --vid-pid c0de:cafe
just py --rtt STM32G0B1RETx --elf fw.elf       # over RTT, the ELF makes attaching fast
just py --api examples/blinky_api              # API from source: device without introspection, or offline
just py --help

Relative paths are resolved from the directory just was run in.

items.title: Connecting
items.text:
import wire_weaver as ww

print(ww.list_devices())                       # connected USB devices, one line each
dev = ww.connect(vid_pid=(0xc0de, 0xcafe), timeout=1.0)
dev.info                                       # API, link and protocol versions reported by the device
dev                                            # resource tree with signatures and docs
dev.disconnect()                               # or `with ww.connect(...) as dev:`

connect() takes keyword arguments only. A USB device is used unless rtt is given; all given filters must match:

Argument Selects vid_pid=(vid, pid) USB vendor and product ID serial, serial_contains USB serial number user_label user label reported by the device product_contains, manufacturer_contains USB product / manufacturer string implements_api=("my_api", ">=0.2") API crate name and a SemVer requirement rtt="STM32G0B1RETx" RTT over a debug probe, probe-rs chip name rtt_elf="fw.elf", rtt_speed_hz firmware ELF to take the RTT control block address from, probe speed timeout default request timeout in seconds api API from load_api(), for a device with introspection disabled

The introspection data is cached in ~/.wire_weaver/, so reconnecting to a device with the same API is quick. Without rtt_elf, RTT attaching scans the target RAM for the control block, see RTT.

items.title: Using the API
items.text:
Resources are attributes, their repr() shows the tree with signatures and the first doc line, and dir() lists them for tab completion. For the Dynamic trait from tests/dynamic_api:

>>> dev
Dynamic
  no_args()
  add(a: u32, b: i16) -> i64
  echo(value: Everything) -> Everything
  check(x: Option<u8>) -> Result<u8, CheckError>
  rw speed: u16
  rw everything: Everything
  rw flagged: Flagged
  channel[]: Channel
>>> dev.channel[0]
channel[0]: Channel
  rw gain: f32
  id() -> u32

dev.no_args()
dev.add(40, b=-2)                      # positional or keyword arguments
dev.speed.write(1500)                  # properties
dev.speed.read(timeout=5)              # timeout overrides the default for one request
dev.channel.valid_indices()            # arrays: indices the device accepts, e.g. [0, 1, 2]
dev.channel[1].gain.write(0.5)

with dev.samples as samples:           # stream from the device: open(), iterate or recv(), close()
    for s in samples:
        ...
dev.samples.recv(timeout=1)            # after open(): next item, TimeoutError if none
dev.samples.try_recv()                 # next item if one is already received, None otherwise

with dev.commands as sink:             # stream to the device (sink): open(), send(), close()
    sink.send({"Move": {"x": 1, "y": 2}})

items.title: Counted and reliable streams
items.text:
A stream marked counted or reliable in the API (its signature says so) gives every item a position, reports what was lost and where, and can be resumed from a saved cursor (Stream reliability):

s = dev.samples
s.open(rate=1000, ack="explicit")      # the stream function's arguments; returns its result, an Err raises RemoteError
                                       # open(cursor=saved) after a restart; ack="receive" is the default
while True:
    ev = s.recv_event(timeout=1)       # dict: kind "item", "gap", "resumed", "backfill_done", "disconnected", "closed"
    if ev["kind"] == "item":
        write(ev["pos"], ev["t"], ev["value"])  # t: device time in seconds, or None
        s.ack(ev["pos"] + ev["units"])          # explicit: the device may free it now
        save_cursor(s.cursor)                   # (session, pos), with the data
    elif ev["kind"] == "gap":
        print(f'{ev["units"]} lost at {ev["at"]} ({ev["cause"]})')  # device, link, store or host
s.stats                                # received, lost by cause, duplicates, queued ...

recv() and iterating return values only, gaps are counted in stats. A resumed reliable stream delivers the latest values at once (run "live") and the backlog beside them (run "backfill"), each in order.

Every resource also has doc (its doc comment), path (e.g. channel[2].gain) and, except traits, signature. Use dev["name"] for a resource named like one of the Device attributes (api, info, disconnect).

Blocking calls release the GIL, and waiting on a stream can be interrupted with Ctrl+C.

items.title: Errors
items.text:
• A method returning Result<T, E> returns T, or raises ww.RemoteError with E in its value attribute.
  • A request without a reply raises TimeoutError.
  • Connection, protocol and device errors raise ww.WireWeaverError (RemoteError is a subclass of it).
  • Values that don't fit the API types raise TypeError or ValueError before anything is sent, e.g. add() argument 'a': -1 is out of range for u32.

items.title: Values
items.text: WireWeaver Python bool bool integers, UNib32, u4, nib int (range is checked) f32, f64 float (int accepted) String, &str str Vec<u8>, [u8; N] bytes (bytearray or a list of ints accepted) Vec<T>, [T; N] list (any iterable accepted) tuple tuple struct with named fields dict (dataclass, namedtuple or an object with attributes accepted) tuple struct tuple, a single field one is its value enum unit variant "Variant" enum variant with fields {"Variant": fields}, fields as for a struct Option<T> None or T, a missing Option field is None Result<T, E> {"Ok": T} or {"Err": E} Range, RangeInclusive (start, end) (range with step 1 accepted)

items.title: API from source, offline use
items.text:
A device with introspection disabled needs its API from the crate source:

api = ww.load_api("path/to/my_api", "MyApi")   # trait name is needed if the crate has several
dev = ww.connect(api=api)

load_api() alone works without a device: browse the API the same way, and serialize values to see what goes over the wire, or decode captured bytes:

>>> api = ww.load_api("tests/dynamic_api", "Dynamic")
>>> api.add.encode_args(40, b=-2).hex()
'28000000feff'
>>> api.speed.encode(1500)
b'\xdc\x05'
>>> api.speed.decode(b"\xdc\x05")
1500
>>> api.check.decode_return(b"\x00\x00\x01")
{'Err': 'TooBig'}

Methods have encode_args() / decode_return(), properties encode() / decode(), streams decode() and sinks encode(). Calling a resource of an offline API raises WireWeaverError.

items.title: Not supported yet
items.text:
• f16, UN/IN and LEB128 numbers.
  • Typed (non-integer) array indices, property write errors (not decoded, same as generated clients), property observation.
  • asyncio: calls block the calling thread (with the GIL released).

items.title: Built-in types
items.text:
• Boolean (one-bit alignment): bool
  • Discrete numbers:
    • Signed (one-byte alignment): i8, i16, i32, i64, i128
    • Unsigned (one-byte alignment): u8, u16, u32, u64, u128
    • Unsigned (four-bit alignment): nib
    • Signed and unsigned (one-bit alignment): u1, u2, u3, ... ub64, i2 ... ib64
      • u8 is byte-aligned, while ub8 is bit-aligned
      • In Rust: U1..U64 and I2..I64 (shrink_wrap::un, in the prelude), backed by the smallest standard integer, with checked constructors (U7::new(x), U7::try_from(x)) and .value() / u8::from(..).
